hooks.text: Scientists turned planet Earth into one giant radio dish.
How do you photograph an object forty billion kilometers wide?
Scientists photographed a black hole using zero space telescopes.

title: How Scientists Photographed a Monster Black Hole
description: In 2019, astronomers unveiled humanity's first photo of a supermassive black hole spanning 40 billion kilometers.

beats.text: Scientists turned planet Earth into one giant radio dish.
beats.visual: Illustration of Event Horizon Telescope network forming an Earth-sized virtual dish, 2019
queries: Event Horizon Telescope Earth network diagram

beats.text: Eight observatories targeted a galaxy 55 million light-years away.
beats.visual: ALMA radio telescope antennas on the Chajnantor plateau in Chile, 2017

beats.text: Every dish synchronized its recordings using atomic clocks.
beats.visual: Hydrogen maser atomic clock at a radio astronomy observatory, 2017

beats.text: But the raw data was way too massive for the internet.
beats.visual: Bank of high-density hard drive storage modules for radio astronomy data, 2017
queries: EHT hard drive banks MIT Haystack

beats.text: Engineers had to fly petabytes of hard drives on airplanes.
beats.visual: Transport crates of EHT hard drives loaded for airplane delivery from Antarctica, 2017
queries: EHT South Pole Telescope hard drives shipment

beats.text: Supercomputers processed the data into humanity's first black hole image.
beats.visual: First direct image of the Messier 87 black hole shadow and accretion ring, 2019
queries: First direct image of a black hole EHT 2019

beats.text: The shadow spans nearly forty billion kilometers across.
beats.visual: Polarized light view of the Messier 87 black hole showing magnetic field structure, 2021
queries: M87 black hole polarized light EHT

beats.text: Its ring of light could swallow our entire solar system.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a supermassive black hole swallowing surrounding material, 2019
queries: Supermassive black hole accretion disk ESO illustration
Black hole event horizon NASA artist concept

beats.text: No single telescope on Earth was big enough.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope view of supergiant galaxy Messier 87 and its jet, 1998

better_than_last: Built around the physical delivery mystery of petabyte data hard drives on airplanes to create middle beat intrigue before revealing the monster scale payoff.
